summary: ```markdown # CLO 2025 Academic Month Group Research: Inspiring Digital Fashion Imagination ## Introduction I am very happy to be able to share with you some of our discussions about the future development direction and possibilities in the digital fashion field. I am also very grateful for the invitation of the organizer. The topic I am going to share with you today is about the imagination of digital fashion. The moderator just introduced it to me, so I won't go into too much detail about it. ## Course Overview Our course is actually a special design course for the third grade of the Chinese Academy of Fine Arts. It is also the first time for the Chinese Academy of Fine Arts to open a fashion design school in recent years. In this course, the students do not have any software-based skills. In the previous period, they did not have any courses related to software. This course is about seven weeks long. ### Guiding Students How to guide students in this limited time of seven weeks? It is a relatively big problem for us to create a multi-dimensional project based on these software-based students. In addition, we are designing the initial design of this course, focusing on the core problems of the first period, which is the possibility of digitalization in the future of the fashion field. ## Digital Fashion Exploration We would like to combine these digitalized, virtual, and different directions to explore whether there are more possibilities in addition to virtual fashion, virtual showrooms, or commercial brands. We chose to use teamwork to teach the form and the problems that appear in our entire workflow and work process. ### Historical Context First of all, we lead students to learn about the historical origins of digital fashion, cultural evolution, technical development, and the impact of artificial intelligence on the trend of fashion in the future. This aims to open up the imagination of students in the information age and provide a new understanding of fashion design. ## Course Structure This course is designed to break down the concepts of digitalized media and the real physical world. We aim to make digitalized fashion design into an imaginative collection for students and systematically establish the creative thinking logic of students' personal digitalized fashion design. The students will complete the digitalized fashion series and the display of digitalized application scenarios in the form of collaborative cooperation by learning from the software mentioned earlier. ### Final Presentation At the end of the seventh week, we held a small exhibition in the school. Some groups focused more on food interaction, while others focused more on virtual interaction. In the video we just saw, they focused more on virtual interaction and presented different forms of content produced for different projects. ## Faculty Overview These are some of our teachers. They are all artists and professional designers who have been growing in the fashion industry for many years. Percy is a modern and advanced digital artist, mainly responsible for the teaching of AIGC and Nomad. Yaya created a brand called Elter, which is a virtual fashion brand. At the time, it was in VVS Westwood, the design headquarters in London, and it was designed by a 3D fashion designer. ### Faculty Expertise - **Mr. Qi Haoran**: A teacher biased towards C4D scene modeling direction. - **Mr. Maruyama**: Responsible for the interaction direction, with nearly 10 years of experience in interaction teaching. In our entire interaction teaching process, Mr. Ma noted that there are a lot of problems he has not encountered in his teaching throughout the years. Our students have no basis for these software applications, so they do not have limitations or predictions about what they can do or cannot do. ## Teaching Methodology The entire course began with a significant lecture where each teacher shared their own experiences and insights from their fields of deep learning, discussing current trends and future development possibilities. ### Mini Projects During the first week, students worked on mini projects after a week of software learning. The group projects are essential for teamwork. The objective condition limitation mentioned earlier is that the students have no basis for this software, and many do not have the necessary equipment, particularly for rendering. #### Resourcefulness and Collaboration In the production process, some students may go to a friend's game company to use professional computers with higher configurations for rendering. This process also helps students develop future social skills, such as dealing with interpersonal relationships in teamwork and maximizing both their personal value and that of the team. ## Challenges Faced Students may encounter team members who lack certain skills, necessitating adjustments in the final production form. For example, some groups may involve programming, requiring collaboration with students skilled in that area. Moreover, we invited industry mentors who sometimes could not be present on-site for teaching, leading to online teaching arrangements. ### Online Learning Resources In the early stages of this course, we provided students with online course links, enabling them to mobilize their subjective energy for software learning. A core point discussed with Professor Percy is that the virtual world differs from the real world; it has no limitations and allows for subversive design. This encourages students to spread their imagination and creativity. ## Project Presentation The video presentation showcased a project about an upside-down world—an opposite to the real world. The students conducted research on the meanings of being upside-down, leading to innovative designs. ### Student Designs This is a draft of the design for the entire computer world at the time, resembling a multi-dimensional cube. Each of the four students created rooms, each with its own story, reflected in their designs of virtual clothing. - **First Student**: A sensitive and warm-hearted girl whose designs relate to her childhood and family, primarily using Qo3D technology. - **Second Student**: Unique clothing designs showcasing her strong personality. - **Third Student**: Active and vibrant designs. - **Fourth Student**: Final design contributions from all students. ## Interactive Elements The projects included interactive components, such as: - A display where audience gestures influence the patterns on clothing and scenery. - An interactive accessory that changes light speed in response to the user’s heart rate. ### Project Overview In summary, the projects explored various themes, including the integration of traditional patterns with modern interactive forms. The application of AIGC, particularly through Stable Diffusion software, allowed students to create a database of their designs and generate new possibilities. Thank you! ```
